term: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association (NYSRPA) v. Bruen (2022)
definition: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association (NYSRPA) v. Bruen, 597 U.S. 1 (2022) is an influential U.S. Supreme Court case interpreting the Second Amendment right to bear arms as it relates to firearms permit restrictions. Bruen eliminated “may-issue” permit laws for public carry weapons and required states with permit or licenses laws to operate on a “shall-issue” basis. The holding in Bruen reaffirmed the historical analysis precedent set in District of Columbia v. Heller, 554 U.S. 570 (2008) and prohibits the use of “means-end” tests when evaluating the constitutionality of gun control legislation. Facts Bruen involved a New York gun control law requiring citizens to obtain a permit to carry a concealed firearm outside of their home. The applicant had to show proper cause for the special need to carry. Permits were issued on a “may-issue” basis, meaning the issuing agencies determined whether the applicant had shown “proper cause” and had a final say on whether to grant such a license. Thus, the government/issuing agency could deny the application if they did not feel the applicant had proper cause, even if the applicant satisfied all other objective standards. Two parties challenged this law in court after government officials deemed their general desires for self-protection were insufficient to establish a heightened need to carry outside of their home and denied their public concealed carry permit application. Decision Justice Thomas delivered the majority opinion. The Supreme Court concluded that the New York law was unconstitutional because it prevented law-abiding citizens from exercising their Second Amendment right to bear arms in public. The Court took issue with New York’s “may-issue” licensing system and stated that it allowed the state governments to deny citizens the opportunity to exercise their right to bear arms at their discretion. This “may-issue” concept contradicted District of Columbia v. Heller, which stated the Second Amendment guarantees an individual the right to possess arms for the purposes of self-defense.
